assessments.reasoning: The separate publisher_terms acquisition returned the same pinned Markdown URL as publisher_heading and independently reported 4563 bytes and source-wide SHA-256 c0ea4a896d2c8c394b29f9427589996db826cd501c512279ff0ed3ef48fabbe5, matching the record's provenance. Its Notices range [992, 1347) reports SHA-256 55fcb55d4a52452475e6afe93cf8c9fd6cb28ef08a369a88fc85e9a6c3ffb736. The delivered text establishes the recipient trigger, the alternative between terms and URL, and the additional requirement for qualifying licensor-supplied lines. The heading supplies the referenced URL, and the surrounding software terms supply the distribution context.

challenge.method: Tested partial copies, delivery of the official URL in place of the terms, cases with and without a licensor-supplied qualifying line, the illustrative notice, and the separate software distribution grant.
challenge.results: A partial copy triggers the same requirement. Delivering https://polyformproject.org/licenses/noncommercial/1.0.0 satisfies the terms-or-URL component. A qualifying line supplied with the software must also be delivered. If the licensor supplied zero qualifying lines, the recipient still needs the terms or URL and there are zero notice lines to copy. The Yoyodyne example illustrates the format. An actual obligation to copy that line depends on the licensor supplying it with the software. The Distribution License provides the separate grant, and notice delivery alone does not establish permission. The tested cases reveal no material contradiction.

limitations: Actual compliance depends on which software was supplied, which lines the licensor supplied with it, and what the recipient received.
The finding addresses notice delivery. Whether a particular distribution is permitted requires separate assessment.
Integrity checks use the fresh tool-reported measurements and inspection of the delivered bytes and text.
